title: unified-rollouts: enhanced observability and rollback workflow improvements for canary/AB/shadow
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: Improve rollback reliability and visibility for unified rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow). Recent incidents showed insufficient signal coverage and unclear rollback triggers for multi-metric/quorum-driven rollouts. This PR adds enhanced telemetry, clearer metric naming, quorum-aware metric aggregation, and tight integration between observability signals and the automated rollback engine.

Summary of changes: 1) Expose new rollout telemetry metrics (rollout.stage_latency_ms, rollout.request_error_rate, rollout.quality_regressions, rollout.metric_quorum_status) and instrument per-route + per-model tags. 2) Implement a quorum-aware aggregator used by the autorollback engine to evaluate composite conditions (supports AND/OR thresholds and weighted metrics). 3) Add observability adapters that emit structured events for preflight and staged shadow probing so the console can render per-stage histograms and failure digests. 4) Add new alerting rules and dashboards in observability-pack for easier debugging and SLI/SLO alignment. 5) Extend e2e preflight tests and add targeted unit tests for metric aggregation and rollback decision paths. 6) Documentation updates in redwood-docs describing metric semantics and guidance for creating safe rollback policies.

Checklist: - [x] Metrics emitted with stable names and tags - [x] Quorum aggregation implementation covered by unit tests - [x] End-to-end preflight tests for staged shadow + canary - [x] Updated dashboards and alert rules - [x] Docs updated with examples and recommended policy templates

Testing: Local unit tests for aggregator logic (coverage ~95%). Added integration test that simulates a progressive canary with injected error signals; validates that autorollback fires when composite metric threshold + quorum are met and does not fire when quorum is not satisfied. CI flake observed on initial run (one e2e timing test) was fixed by increasing tolerances and adding a deterministic seed for the simulated load generator. All CI checks passed on final run.

Backward compatibility and safety: Metric names are additive and existing rollout policies continue to work. The quorum aggregator is opt-in via a rollout policy flag (quorum: {enabled: true}) so customers must explicitly opt their policies to the new behavior. No breaking API changes.

Rollout plan: Merge to main behind feature flag rollout.observability. After staged dogfood in dedicated environment for 2 weeks, flip feature flag for all internal tenants, then gradual customer opt-ins via console templates.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on metric naming consistency, aggregation semantics, and performance implications of the aggregator (hot-path checks are cached and use incremental windows). See commits for implementation details.
